summary.headline: Elgi FY26 revenue grew about 12% and PBT about 17%, but management flagged metal-commodity cost pressure with a 2.5–3% price correction planned for June.
summary.overview: Management said FY26 sales grew about 12% and PBT about 17%, with consolidated revenue close to 4,000 crore, though EBITDA was held back by employee costs (up 16%, including a one-time settlement and US/Europe shared-service reorganisation) and product mix. Volume growth averaged 3–4% across verticals, with pricing largely flat for the year apart from the Demand=Match launch in September. Management expects Q1 FY27 top-line growth similar to or slightly above FY26 and bottom-line growth roughly in line in percentage terms. Europe was loss-making for FY26 and broke even in Q4, and management said it expects marginal profitability there. The company said it is planning a price correction in June as most of the projected material-cost increase has already happened in Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: increase stated; management said underlying EBITDA should have been about 2,100 million before employee cost impact
financial_highlights.change: employee cost +16% YoY; other expenses +8% YoY

financial_highlights.value: loss for FY26 (amount not disclosed); breakeven in Q4 FY26
100% of EBITDA converted to cash, even normalised for property sale proceeds

segments.name: Compressors (India vs rest of world)
segments.commentary: Compressor sales split roughly 50-50 between India and rest of world, with about 90-10 as a rough distribution within the compressor business as described. Sales mix between compressors and automotive equipment described as stable.

segments.name: Regions
segments.commentary: All regions except Australia and Southeast Asia grew in FY26. America described as doing very well, with industrial strong and distribution improving in the last two quarters; Europe went through cost realignment and is now sized to its business.

segments.name: Vacuum (licence with DVP)
segments.commentary: Early-stage entry via a licence agreement with DVP; management described it as a 10–12 year programme, not a near-term growth driver.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27: top-line growth expected to be similar to or slightly better than FY26 growth; bottom-line growth roughly the same in percentage terms.
Price correction of about 2.5–3% (planned in FY27 cost projections) to be taken in June 2026, as close to 80% of projected material-cost increase has already occurred in Q1.
Commodity prices: comfortable until June; reassessing scenarios thereafter.
Europe expected to be marginally profitable in the year ahead; worst case was breakeven.
Capex FY27 about 200 crore (about 120–130 crore for the factory shift to the new plant and about 70 crore balancing capex). FY26 capex was about 1.5 billion.
Inventory reduction to continue into FY27; forecast accuracy currently 60–70%, target about 90%.
Low-cost compressor range targeted for India launch in September 2026; rest of world launch next year.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex planned at about 200 crore: about 120–130 crore for progressive shift of the factory from city to new plant, and about 70 crore of balancing capex.
Management said desire to spend is higher than capacity to spend on capex.
No new capex in Europe planned; growth to come organically, with Germany as a new market to enter.
Motor business: more than 95% of motors made in-house; new motor range planned to launch in the next 1–1.5 years.
demand_pricing: Inquiry levels strong across India; conversion timing lengthening, which management views as a caution signal.
West Asia conflict and energy/commodity prices cited as the main source of customer caution, not Indian capability.
Pricing: FY26 price realisation largely flat; Demand=Match launched September 2025 with small contribution so far; FX a significant contributor.
Metal commodity prices rising weekly/monthly; company will correct prices in June when demand allows.
Competition: Chinese low-cost players churning the bottom end globally; industry structure otherwise stable.
US tariffs now about 25% (down from 50%), applying to exports from Italy and India; refund of past tariffs under discussion with agencies.
Europe market growth muted due to Ukraine war, energy crisis, inflation and unemployment.

qa_highlights.question: What was blended realisation growth in FY26 and what price increase is needed in FY27 to hold gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth averaged 3–4%, pricing was hardly any due to Demand=Match launch in September with small contribution, and FX was a significant contributor. Management had modelled a 2.5–3% price correction, with about 80% of the projected material-cost increase already occurred in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a one-off in other expenses, and was it linked to shared services?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses rose due to India go-to-market investment and IT spend, primarily the PLM investment, not shared-services relocation.

qa_highlights.question: Demand outlook in Indian capex sectors and emerging segments like data centres?
qa_highlights.answer: Inquiries strong; conversion slower due to West Asia uncertainty. No direct data-centre business, but ancillary suppliers needing compressed air are being pursued; solar also cited as an established segment.

qa_highlights.question: Status of US tariffs and market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Tariffs now about 25% (earlier 50%) on Italy and India exports; refund talks are at an early stage.

qa_highlights.question: Industry structure and response to Chinese low-cost players?
qa_highlights.answer: Structure stable except at the bottom end where Chinese players sell low-cost machines globally. Low-cost range designs validated, with India launch targeted for September and rest of world next year.

qa_highlights.question: Europe profitability and growth plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe loss-making for FY26, breakeven in Q4; marginal profitability expected next year. No additional capital for Europe; Germany to be entered organically.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 capex budget?
qa_highlights.answer: About 200 crore in total: 120–130 crore for the factory relocation and about 70 crore of balancing capex.

risks_watch: Metal commodity price volatility; price correction in June may face demand elasticity risk, per management.
West Asia conflict and energy prices affecting customer order conversion and Middle East sales.
Lengthening conversion timelines for orders despite strong inquiries.
US tariff regime uncertain (about 25% currently) and pending refund outcome.
Inventory levels at distribution businesses in Australia and US (including other brands) still to be reduced.
Other expenses and IT/GTM investments to continue for three to four years, weighing on cost structure.
Europe profitability, with breakeven only reached in Q4 FY26.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and cash generation, with a cautious tone on commodity costs, West Asia uncertainty and order conversion timing. Management was evasive on specific numbers, deferring Forex gains, Europe's FY loss amount and the blended realisation figure to follow-up.
key_quotes: We are not worried about the competitive reality because these commodity prices are affecting pretty much everyone.
So, what we need to do now is take stock of what will be the future and correct prices, which is what we will do in the month of June.
We are not interested in investing more capital in Europe at this point in time.
We need to, we are at an accuracy level of maybe 60, 70 percent. We need to move it to around 90, then we'll be a lot more comfortable in terms of sustaining this in the future.
